- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

12	- Nonemptiness and density of the reduced-support open on every relevant geometric fibre.
13	- CE relative-canonical normalization and the identification W_5≅ω_C^2(-D).

15	## Mathematical constraints
16	
17	- For every reduced H_k, infer dim(I|_{H_k})=15+k-1. [reason: A P^{k-1}-bundle has dimension dim(H_k)+k-1. The base need not have dimension 15; in particular dim(H_4)≤14.]
18	- Infer irreducibility of the balanced open H_3 directly from irreducibility of the classical Hurwitz space. [reason: An open splitting stratum need not be dense or irreducible merely because the ambient Hurwitz space is irreducible; density and connectivity of the relevant splitting stratum require proof.]
19	- Infer that every reduced ordered point has trivial stabilizer from the six marked points. [reason: Six fixed points do not exceed the genus-6 bound 2g+2=14, and the available argument controls only a dense open with at least three distinct target images and an unramified mark.]
20	- Infer global finiteness or quasi-finiteness of the forgetful morphism from injectivity over H_3 and fibre dimension at most two over H_4. [reason: A positive upper bound on exceptional fibre dimension does not imply zero-dimensional fibres, so it does not establish quasi-finiteness or the asserted finite-fibre image-dimension argument.]
21	- Infer that a morphism of stacks is a monomorphism from injectivity on geometric points and injectivity on automorphism groups. [reason: A stack monomorphism requires full faithfulness on objects over every base scheme; fibrewise recovery does not control families, especially where π_*(ω(-Γ)) changes rank.]
22	- Infer nonempty distinct-support ordered incidence on every fibre from χ(L)=1. [reason: The Euler-characteristic argument yields a nonempty complete Abel–Jacobi fibre in Sym^6, but does not ensure a divisor with six distinct support points.]
23	- Infer Tate or only-Tate local systems from rationality of S_6-representations. [reason: Rational representation theory alone does not determine the geometric monodromy image, Hodge type, weights, or Tate purity of the resulting local systems.]
24	- Identify the relative linear system globally with Proj(π_*L) across h^0-jumping strata or a nonreduced base. [reason: When h^0 jumps, π_*L need not be locally free or commute with base change; reduced constant-rank strata are needed for the projective-bundle identification.]
25	- Infer a closed pure-codimension-four locus and a Gysin map solely from a 17-dimensional constructible image in a 21-dimensional moduli stack. [reason: Constructible image dimension does not imply closedness, purity of codimension, regularity, or the existence of a suitable closed embedding.]
26	- The reduced-support open has image dimension dim(B)+2 merely because the full Abel-Jacobi incidence is a P^2-bundle and the classifying map is injective on geometric points. [reason: The reduced-support locus is only an open subset of the projective bundle and may be empty or fail to dominate a component of B. Injectivity controls fibres where the open exists but does not prove nonemptiness or dominance.]
27	- The relative identities Fit_0(coker(phi))=I_12(phi)=I_6(phi_5) hold over any base carrying an arbitrary relative degree-six divisor. [reason: The filtered relative argument uses six disjoint sections and cohomology-and-base-change hypotheses. Fibrewise rank behavior does not determine nilpotent or Fitting scheme structure for a general relative divisor.]
28	- Constancy of h^0(omega_C(-D)) on the balanced locus is equivalent to excluding every non-primitive degree-four pencil. [reason: The h^0(D)=3 case detects composition through the genus-zero hyperelliptic map. Factorizations through degree-two maps to intermediate curves of positive genus are not excluded by this dichotomy and can retain h^0(D)=2.]
29	- The Riemann-Hurwitz total ramification degree 18 implies that the balanced degree-four cover space has dimension 18-3=15 without further hypotheses. [reason: Total ramification degree equals the number of distinct branch points only for simple ramification. # Mathematical working context (C66-COMP-RANK)

Treat candidates as unproved. Reprove every fact used in the final argument. Constraints below are hard stops: do not walk them again.

## Frontier obligations

- Nonemptiness of the reduced-support open in |L_b| and of the ordered Conf_6 incidence on every balanced geometric fibre.
- Which values of h^0(L) occur on each balanced stratum, and whether h^0(L) is constant on the balanced locus.
- Finite local freeness of the CE equation bundle and its commutation with arbitrary base change, needed for ambient versus intrinsic evaluation agreement.
- Image dimension and codimension in M_{6,6}, together with components, stabilizers, closure, lci/Gysin structure, Hodge/purity data, and Tate type of the exact codimension-13 contribution.
- The dimension and stabilizers of the relevant balanced tetragonal base components, including simple branching.
- Nonemptiness and density of the reduced-support open on every relevant geometric fibre.
- CE relative-canonical normalization and the identification W_5≅ω_C^2(-D).

## Mathematical constraints

- For every reduced H_k, infer dim(I|_{H_k})=15+k-1. [reason: A P^{k-1}-bundle has dimension dim(H_k)+k-1. The base need not have dimension 15; in particular dim(H_4)≤14.]
- Infer irreducibility of the balanced open H_3 directly from irreducibility of the classical Hurwitz space. [reason: An open splitting stratum need not be dense or irreducible merely because the ambient Hurwitz space is irreducible; density and connectivity of the relevant splitting stratum require proof.]
- Infer that every reduced ordered point has trivial stabilizer from the six marked points. [reason: Six fixed points do not exceed the genus-6 bound 2g+2=14, and the available argument controls only a dense open with at least three distinct target images and an unramified mark.]
- Infer global finiteness or quasi-finiteness of the forgetful morphism from injectivity over H_3 and fibre dimension at most two over H_4. [reason: A positive upper bound on exceptional fibre dimension does not imply zero-dimensional fibres, so it does not establish quasi-finiteness or the asserted finite-fibre image-dimension argument.]
- Infer that a morphism of stacks is a monomorphism from injectivity on geometric points and injectivity on automorphism groups. [reason: A stack monomorphism requires full faithfulness on objects over every base scheme; fibrewise recovery does not control families, especially where π_*(ω(-Γ)) changes rank.]
- Infer nonempty distinct-support ordered incidence on every fibre from χ(L)=1. [reason: The Euler-characteristic argument yields a nonempty complete Abel–Jacobi fibre in Sym^6, but does not ensure a divisor with six distinct support points.]
- Infer Tate or only-Tate local systems from rationality of S_6-representations. [reason: Rational representation theory alone does not determine the geometric monodromy image, Hodge type, weights, or Tate purity of the resulting local systems.]
- Identify the relative linear system globally with Proj(π_*L) across h^0-jumping strata or a nonreduced base. [reason: When h^0 jumps, π_*L need not be locally free or commute with base change; reduced constant-rank strata are needed for the projective-bundle identification.]
- Infer a closed pure-codimension-four locus and a Gysin map solely from a 17-dimensional constructible image in a 21-dimensional moduli stack. [reason: Constructible image dimension does not imply closedness, purity of codimension, regularity, or the existence of a suitable closed embedding.]
- The reduced-support open has image dimension dim(B)+2 merely because the full Abel-Jacobi incidence is a P^2-bundle and the classifying map is injective on geometric points. [reason: The reduced-support locus is only an open subset of the projective bundle and may be empty or fail to dominate a component of B. Injectivity controls fibres where the open exists but does not prove nonemptiness or dominance.]
- The relative identities Fit_0(coker(phi))=I_12(phi)=I_6(phi_5) hold over any base carrying an arbitrary relative degree-six divisor. [reason: The filtered relative argument uses six disjoint sections and cohomology-and-base-change hypotheses. Fibrewise rank behavior does not determine nilpotent or Fitting scheme structure for a general relative divisor.]
- Constancy of h^0(omega_C(-D)) on the balanced locus is equivalent to excluding every non-primitive degree-four pencil. [reason: The h^0(D)=3 case detects composition through the genus-zero hyperelliptic map. Factorizations through degree-two maps to intermediate curves of positive genus are not excluded by this dichotomy and can retain h^0(D)=2.]
- The Riemann-Hurwitz total ramification degree 18 implies that the balanced degree-four cover space has dimension 18-3=15 without further hypotheses. [reason: Total ramification degree equals the number of distinct branch points only for simple ramification. Collisions and higher ramification change the branch-point count and can alter component dimensions.]
- The equality chi(L)=1 guarantees a reduced effective divisor in |L| and hence a nonempty ordered six-point incidence. [reason: Riemann-Roch guarantees only a nonzero section. Its divisor may have repeated support, and every member of the linear system may contain a non-reduced fixed part.]
- Fibrewise balancedness gives a global splitting W=W_4 direct-sum W_5 over an arbitrary family, permitting block-diagonal minor factorization. [reason: Balancedness supplies a relative Harder-Narasimhan filtration, not a global splitting. The relevant extension class need not vanish over the base.]
- Expected determinantal codimension 6 versus actual codimension 4 implies that the rank-drop locus is nowhere a local complete intersection. [reason: Failure to attain the generic determinantal codimension does not preclude a regular sequence of the actual codimension. A local-complete-intersection conclusion requires depth or conormal calculations.]
- A finite etale S_6-cover contributes only Tate cohomology because every rational irreducible representation of S_6 is defined over Q. [reason: The field of definition of deck-group representations does not control the Hodge type of cohomology with the associated geometric monodromy local systems.]
- From AJ_B≅P(p_*L_B) of pure relative dimension 2 and geometric-point injectivity of the classifying map, conclude unconditionally that the image in M_{6,6} of the reduced-support open of AJ_B has dimension dim B+2 and codimension 19−dim B. [reason: The reduced-support locus is only an open subset of the P^2-bundle AJ_B. Open subsets of fibres can be empty: without a proved reduced member of |L| on each relevant component, the image-dimension claim need not hold. Geometric-point injectivity does not force nonemptiness of that open.]
- Assert Fit_0(coker φ)=I_12(φ)=I_6(φ_5) and I_11(φ)=O_B for an arbitrary base carrying a balanced family with any relative degree-6 divisor Γ. [reason: The filtered snake/Fitting argument uses Γ realized by (or reduced to) six disjoint sections and the vanishings deg W_4>2g−2 and deg W_4(−Γ)>2g−2. Fibrewise corank ≤1 is strictly weaker than those scheme-theoretic Fitting equalities over arbitrary bases.]
- Identify constancy of h^0(ω_C(−D))=3 on the balanced locus with exclusion of all non-primitive degree-4 pencils. [reason: h^0(O_C(D))=3 characterises covers factoring through the hyperelliptic map (intermediate genus 0). Degree-4 covers through an intermediate curve of genus 1, 2, or 3 still have h^0(O_C(D))=2; constancy uses only exclusion of the hyperelliptic case.]
- Infer local complete intersection, smoothness, closedness, Gysin, purity, or Tate-type conclusions from the excess identity excess = h^1(L)=2 alone. [reason: The excess identity only compares expected determinantal fibre dimension 0 with actual dim|L|=2; it does not control ideal depth, conormal sheaves, embedding dimension, or Hodge/Tate type.]
- Treating R^1 pi_* Q of the universal punctured curve as pure of weight 1 and using weight p as the floor at cohomological degree p. [reason: R^1 pi_* Q is an extension of a weight-2 Tate system by a weight-1 system, hence mixed of weights 1 and 2; the actual weight floor for H^p(base; L) is p+1, so a pure-weight-1 treatment is off by exactly one unit of weight and targets an identically zero group.]
- Identifying the top-weight graph-complex corner gr^W_0 H^*_c(M_{g,n}), equivalently gr^W_{2d}H^*(M_{g,n}), with the lowest-weight target gr^W_{2d-16}H^{2d-16}(M_{g,n})(d). [reason: The two corners coincide only if 2d = 2d-16, which never holds; for (6,6) the top-weight corner has weight 42 while the target has weight 26, and no twist or dimension shift reconciles distinct weights.]
- Bounding pure-weight cohomology of a local system on the total space from a gonality or Brill-Noether stratification of the base by evaluating only the open stratum. [reason: Such a bound requires the localization spectral sequence with codimension shifts and Tate twists (a codimension-4 stratum contributes through degree p-8 cohomology twisted by Q(-4)) and control of its differentials; restriction to the open stratum is in general neither injective nor surjective.]
- Normalizing the non-separating boundary divisor of Mbar_{6,6} by Mbar_{5,7}. [reason: Normalization of a non-separating node drops the genus by one and adds two legs at the node, giving 6+2 = 8 legs; dim Mbar_{5,7} = 19 is not 21-1 = 20, so Mbar_{5,7} cannot be the codimension-one boundary normalization.]
- Identifying a relative linear system with Proj(pi_*L) without qualification when h^0(L) jumps. [reason: Proj(pi_*L) has the correct fibres only over the open where h^0(L) is constant; a global identification requires cohomology-and-base-change hypotheses or a compatible divisor/Hilbert or Abel-Jacobi construction.]
- Concluding scheme-theoretic equality of the evaluation-obstruction locus and an Abel-Jacobi incidence locus from a fibrewise equivalence between nonvanishing of an obstruction space and triviality of a degree-zero line bundle. 31	  "theorem_statement": "Let k be a field of characteristic zero, B a locally Noetherian k-scheme, pi:C->B a smooth proper morphism with geometrically connected genus-g fibres, and x_1,...,x_n:B->C pairwise disjoint sections with n>=1 and Gamma=sum x_i(B). Let 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 be exact on C, with W_4,W_5 invertible, W locally free of rank two, and constant fibre degrees d_4,d_5 satisfying d_4-n>2g-2 and d_5-n=2g-2. Put phi:pi_*W->pi_*(W|Gamma), N=omega_{C/B} tensor W_5^vee(Gamma), P=Pic^0_{C/B}, a_N:B->P, and let e:B->P be the identity. Then Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e; hence the intrinsic evaluation-failure scheme is exactly a_N^{-1}(e(B)), formation commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change, the scheme represents relative triviality of N, and the identity descends along smooth atlases to locally Noetherian algebraic stacks. For the ambient comparison, additionally let s:P1_B->B, let p:X=P_{P1_B}(E^vee)->P1_B be a P2-bundle, let gamma:C->P1_B be a finite flat degree-four cover with CE embedding i:C->X, and assume its ideal has the standard degree-four CE resolution 0->O_X(-4) tensor p^*det(F)->O_X(-2) tensor p^*F->I_C->0 for a rank-two relations bundle F. Put q=s composed with p, script-W=O_X(2) tensor p^*F^vee, W=i^*script-W, and assume q_*script-W is finite locally free and commutes with arbitrary base change. If R^1s_*End(F)=0, then the restriction r:q_*script-W->pi_*W is surjective; consequently coker(phi composed with r)=coker(phi) canonically and compatibly with arbitrary base change, and the ambient and intrinsic zeroth Fitting ideals both equal a_N^*I_e. In particular, when (g,n)=(6,6) and every geometric fibre of F is O(4) direct-sum O(5), the canonical filtration induced by the O(5)-subbundle gives d_4=20,d_5=16, the intrinsic map has ranks 26->12, R^1s_*End(F)=0 automatically, and the actual ambient balanced CE evaluation-failure scheme is scheme-theoretically the locus where O_C(Gamma) is relatively isomorphic to W_5 tensor omega_{C/B}^{-1}.",

40	  "summary": "Repairs the ambient overstatement refuted by REV-0106 while retaining the independently confirmed intrinsic proof from ATT-0064. The universal nonreduced Picard calculation gives Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e, and the filtered argument reduces evaluation to W_5 without a global splitting. For the actual ambient CE map, the standard degree-four CE resolution is tensored by script-W and pushed first along the P2-bundle. This gives the exact sequence 0->End(F)->p_*script-W->gamma_*W->0. Pushing along P1_B shows that the sole obstruction to surjectivity of q_*script-W->pi_*W is R^1s_*End(F). The theorem now assumes this vanishing exactly where it is needed. On the fibrewise O(4)+O(5) locus it follows from End(F_b)=O^2+O(1)+O(-1), so the balanced (6,6) ambient and intrinsic cokernels and Fitting schemes agree under arbitrary base change. No ambient assertion is made for the unbalanced counterexamples exposed by REV-0106.",
41	  "argument_markdown": "## 1. Standard relative inputs and source boundary\n\nEvery morphism below is of finite presentation. The curve morphisms are smooth and proper, and all sheaves to which cohomology and base change is applied are locally free. Thus their derived pushforwards are perfect and commute with arbitrary base change. For a relative curve, top cohomology R^1 commutes with arbitrary base change; if all its geometric fibres vanish, the sheaf vanishes by Nakayama, and degree-zero pushforward is then locally free and base-change-compatible. We also use relative duality R^1pi_*omega_{C/B}=O_B, base change for Fitting ideals, invariance of Fit_0 under an invertible twist, deformation theory T_e Pic^0=R^1pi_*O_C, fibrewise Serre duality, and Nakayama. The section x_1 rigidifies Pic_{C/B}, so Pic^0 is an abelian B-scheme admitting a Poincare bundle, unique up to a line bundle pulled back from Pic^0.\n\nThe immutable packet is proof/packets/generated/C66-001-v4-39e87ba7e3784b68.md. From SRC-0004 we use only the degree-four CE convention W_f=(O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-f))|C and the degree formula deg(W_f)=4g+12-4f. The ambient restriction-surjectivity assertion is not imported from SRC-0004. It is proved in Section 8 from the standard CE ideal resolution explicitly included among the theorem hypotheses.\n\n## 2. Ranks and universal Picard cokernel\n\nThe hypotheses imply deg(W_4)>2g-2 and deg(W_5)=2g-2+n>2g-2. Fibrewise Serre duality gives H^1(W_4)=H^1(W_5)=0, hence R^1pi_*W=0. Therefore pi_*W is locally free, commutes with arbitrary base change, and has rank d_4+d_5+2-2g. Since Gamma is the disjoint union of n sections, pi_*(W|Gamma) is locally free of rank 2n. Thus Fit_0(coker phi)=I_{2n}(phi).\n\nPut P=Pic^0_{C/B}, p_C:C_P->P, Gamma_P=Gamma times_B P, and choose a Poincare bundle Q on C_P. Set L_univ=omega_{C_P/P}(Gamma_P) tensor Q^{-1}. Its fibre degree is 2g-2+n, so R^1p_C*L_univ=0, p_C*L_univ is locally free of rank g+n-1, and p_C*(L_univ|Gamma_P) is locally free of rank n, all with arbitrary base change. If Phi is evaluation and J=Fit_0(coker Phi), the sequence 0->omega tensor Q^{-1}->L_univ->L_univ|Gamma_P->0 gives\n\ncoker Phi = R^1p_C*(omega tensor Q^{-1}). (2.1)\n\nThe right side is top cohomology and commutes with arbitrary base change.\n\n## 3. The inclusion J subset I_e\n\nLet e:B->P be the identity and I_e its ideal. Since e^*Q=pi^*M_0 for an invertible M_0 on B, base change in (2.1) gives coker(e^*Phi)=R^1pi_*omega tensor M_0^{-1}=M_0^{-1}. Its zeroth Fitting ideal is zero. Hence e^*J=0, equivalently J subset I_e. This is an ideal containment over an arbitrary possibly nonreduced B, not a support calculation.\n\n## 4. The reverse inclusion I_e subset J\n\nAt a point z outside e(B), with residue field K, (2.1) and Serre duality give (coker Phi) tensor K=H^1(omega tensor Q_z^{-1})=H^0(Q_z)^vee=0: a degree-zero line bundle on a geometrically integral proper curve has a nonzero section only when it is trivial, and z is not the identity. Nakayama gives J_z=O_{P,z}=I_{e,z}.\n\nNow let z=e(b), kappa=k(b), R=O_{P,z}, I=I_{e,z}, and A=R/I=O_{B,b}. For each nonzero relative tangent xi in H^1(C_kappa,O), pull Q^{-1} back along the corresponding dual-number arc i_xi:Spec(kappa[eps])->P_b. As an O_{C_kappa}-module the pullback is an extension 0->O->Q_xi^{-1}->O->0 with class -xi. After tensoring by omega, the connecting map H^0(omega)->H^1(omega)=kappa is cup product with -xi. The Serre pairing is perfect, so this map is nonzero and therefore surjective. The remaining long exact sequence gives H^1(omega tensor Q_xi^{-1})=kappa as a kappa[eps]-module killed by eps. Consequently i_xi^*J=(eps).\n\nBecause J subset I, the last equality says that every nonzero functional xi on the conormal fibre (I/I^2) tensor_A kappa is nonzero on the image of J. The annihilator of that image is therefore zero, so finite-dimensional duality makes the image all of the conormal fibre. If V is the A-submodule of I/I^2 generated by J, Nakayama gives V=I/I^2, hence I=J+I^2. The finite R-module I/J then satisfies I/J=I(I/J), and I lies in the maximal ideal of R; a second Nakayama gives I/J=0. Thus I=J on e(B), and together with the off-section computation,\n\nJ=I_e. (4.1)\n\n## 5. Filtered reduction to W_5\n\nTensoring 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 with O_Gamma stays exact because W_5 is locally free. Pushforward along the affine finite morphism Gamma->B is exact. The upper pushforward row is exact because R^1pi_*W_4=0. Also coker(pi_*W_4->pi_*(W_4|Gamma))=R^1pi_*(W_4(-Gamma))=0, since d_4-n>2g-2. The snake lemma therefore gives canonically\n\ncoker(phi)=coker(phi_5)=R^1pi_*(W_5(-Gamma)). (5.1)\n\nNo splitting of W is used.\n\n## 6. Intrinsic Abel-Jacobi identity, base change, and stacks\n\nSet N=omega tensor W_5^vee(Gamma). It has fibre degree zero and W_5(-Gamma)=omega tensor N^{-1}. Let a_N:B->P classify N. For an invertible M on B, (id_C,a_N)^*Q=N tensor pi^*M. Pulling (2.1) back along a_N and using top-degree base change yields a_N^*(coker Phi)=R^1pi_*(omega tensor N^{-1}) tensor M^{-1}=coker(phi_5) tensor M^{-1}. From Fitting base change, invertible-twist invariance, (5.1), and (4.1),\n\nFit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*J=a_N^*I_e. (6.1)\n\nThus the intrinsic failure scheme is the scheme-theoretic fibre a_N^{-1}(e(B)). All constructions commute with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change. For T->B, the pullback ideal vanishes exactly when a_{N_T} factors through e_T, equivalently, by the x_1-rigidification, when N_T=pi_T^*M_T for an invertible M_T on T. On a locally Noetherian algebraic stack carrying the data, (6.1) holds on a smooth atlas and its double overlap; effective descent of quasi-coherent ideals and the smooth-local T-point criterion give the identical closed substack. No coarse-space assertion is made.\n\n## 7. Canonical balanced filtration and degrees\n\nLet s:P1_B->B and suppose every geometric fibre of F is O(4)+O(5). Then F(-5) has fibres O(-1)+O, so s_*F(-5) is invertible, R^1s_*F(-5)=0, and formation commutes with arbitrary base change. The counit s^*s_*F(-5)->F(-5) has constant rank one on every geometric fibre and is a subbundle with locally free quotient. After twisting, 0->L_5:=O(5) tensor s^*s_*F(-5)->F->L_4->0 is exact, with fibre degrees 5 and 4. Dualising, pulling back to C, and twisting by O_X(2)|C gives 0->W_4->W->W_5->0, where SRC-0004 gives deg(W_4)=20 and deg(W_5)=16 at g=6. For n=6, 20-6=14>10 and 16-6=10=2g-2. Hence phi has ranks 20+16+2-12=26 to 12, and (6.1) identifies its intrinsic failure scheme with relative isomorphism O_C(Gamma)=W_5 tensor omega^{-1}.\n\n## 8. Direct ambient CE comparison and the exact obstruction\n\nRetain the notation in the theorem. The standard CE ideal resolution is\n\n0->O_X(-4) tensor p^*det(F)->O_X(-2) tensor p^*F->I_C->0. (8.1)\n\nTensor (8.1) by script-W=O_X(2) tensor p^*F^vee. Since F has rank two, det(F) tensor F^vee is canonically F. We obtain\n\n0->O_X(-2) tensor p^*F->p^*End(F)->I_C tensor script-W->0. (8.2)\n\nFor a P2-bundle, Rp_*O_X(-2)=0 in every degree, while Rp_*O_X=O_{P1_B}. Projection formula applied to (8.2) therefore gives a canonical derived isomorphism Rp_*(I_C tensor script-W)=End(F), concentrated in degree zero. Also Rp_*script-W=p_*script-W is concentrated in degree zero because O_X(2) has no higher cohomology on P2 fibres. Applying Rp_* to 0->I_C tensor script-W->script-W->i_*W->0 now gives the short exact sequence on P1_B\n\n0->End(F)->p_*script-W->gamma_*W->0. (8.3)\n\nThis is the precise place where the ideal-sheaf twist matters. The irrelevant vanishing H^1(X_b,O_{X_b}) is not used.\n\nApply s_* to (8.3). Since gamma is finite, s_*gamma_*W=pi_*W, and the beginning of the long exact sequence is\n\n0->s_*End(F)->q_*script-W->pi_*W->R^1s_*End(F). (8.4)\n\nUnder the explicit hypothesis R^1s_*End(F)=0, (8.4) proves that r:q_*script-W->pi_*W is surjective. If tilde-phi is ambient evaluation at Gamma, then tilde-phi=phi composed with r; hence im(tilde-phi)=im(phi), and there is a canonical equality coker(tilde-phi)=coker(phi). Both q_*script-W and pi_*W commute with arbitrary base change by hypothesis and Section 2, while the CE resolution and (8.3) are base-change-compatible. A pullback of the surjection r remains surjective, so the cokernel equality is compatible with every locally Noetherian base change. Consequently\n\nFit_0(coker tilde-phi)=Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e. (8.5)\n\nThe equation-bundle/base-change hypothesis alone is deliberately not claimed to imply surjectivity: (8.4) displays the additional obstruction exactly.\n\n## 9. Vanishing of the obstruction on the balanced locus\n\nIf F_b=O(4)+O(5) on a geometric fibre of s, then End(F_b)=O+O+O(1)+O(-1), whose H^1 is zero. Since End(F) is locally free and s is a relative projective line, top-degree cohomology commutes with arbitrary base change. Thus every geometric fibre of the coherent sheaf R^1s_*End(F) is zero; Nakayama gives R^1s_*End(F)=0 on B. The same remains true after arbitrary base change. Therefore Section 8 applies to the balanced family without any global splitting of F. Combining (7.1), (8.5), and the degree computation proves that the actual balanced (6,6) ambient CE failure scheme is exactly the relative incidence O_C(Gamma)=W_5 tensor omega^{-1}, scheme-theoretically and after arbitrary base change.\n\n## 10. Scope and the REV-0106 repair\n\nREV-0106 correctly observed that ATT-0064's broader ambient clause was false: on the equation-bundle open the ambient restriction can have cokernel H^1(P1,End(F)), which is nonzero for sufficiently unbalanced F. This attempt does not assert that clause. The intrinsic theorem remains general under its degree hypotheses; the ambient theorem separately assumes the exact obstruction vanishing, and the target balanced locus proves that vanishing.\n\nProved here are the universal Picard Fitting identity, the filtered reduction, arbitrary base change, stack descent, canonical balanced filtration, balanced degree and rank specialization, the relative CE Koszul comparison, and the balanced ambient-to-intrinsic cokernel equality. SRC-0004 supplies only the CE sign convention and degree formula. No assertion is made about unbalanced ambient comparison, h0 strata, nonemptiness of the reduced-support open, image or closure in M_{6,6}, components, dimension, stabilizers, smoothness, lci/Gysin properties, or Hodge/Tate conclusions.",

I am writing a genus-6, n=6 lemma about the balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl evaluation map phi (ranks 26 -> 12) and the incidence locus Z = {O_C(Gamma) = L} where L = omega_C(-D) has degree 6. My intended new content is exactly these five items:

(a) Fit_1(coker phi) = I_11(phi) = O_B (fibrewise corank is at most 1), so the determinantal stratification has only two strata.
(b) On every balanced geometric fibre, |L| contains a divisor with six pairwise DISTINCT points (nonemptiness/density of the reduced-support open in |L| = P^2), proved by a char-0 Bertini/dual-variety argument plus Clifford to control the fixed part.
(c) Balanced (F = O(4)+O(5)) implies C is not hyperelliptic; and on a hyperelliptic genus-6 curve every degree-4 morphism to P^1 factors through the hyperelliptic map.
(d) Z is smooth over the base of pure relative dimension 2, is a finite etale S_6-torsor over the reduced-support open of the P^2-bundle P(p_*L), and is CLOSED in the ordered configuration space Conf_6(C/H) (while the reduced-support open is NOT closed in P(p_*L)).
(e) Z sits in Conf_6(C/H) as a regular embedding of pure codimension 4, giving a Gysin map; the excess versus the expected determinantal codimension 6 is exactly 2 = h^1(L).

Report back, quoting verbatim with file and approximate line number:
1. Every "mathematical constraint" / blocked-route bullet in those two files that would bind on or forbid any of (a)-(e), especially anything about Bertini or reduced members, hyperelliptic exclusion, Fitting/minor ideals I_11 or I_12, smoothness/lci/regular-embedding/Gysin/purity claims for the incidence, closedness claims, or S_6-cover/etale-torsor claims.
2. Any "established fact" or "reusable computation" in those two files that already states or contradicts any of (a)-(e).
3. Any bullet stating something about h^0(L) jumping, the H_4 / h^0=4 stratum, or dim H_4 <= 14, quoted verbatim.

Be exhaustive on item 1 and terse elsewhere. Quote, do not paraphrase, for item 1. If a file has no relevant bullet for some sub-item, say so explicitly.

# Focused campaign packet: C66-001

- Campaign revision: `4`
- Target context revision: `2`
- Exact target: `W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6})(21)`
- Exact theorem: `The exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.`

## Canonical geometric bottleneck

- Balanced tetragonal splitting: `F=O_{P1}(4) direct-sum O_{P1}(5)`.
- CE line-bundle convention: `W_5 := (O_{P(E^vee)}(2) tensor gamma^*O_{P1}(-5))|_C, the f_2=5 summand of (O(2) tensor gamma^*F^vee)|_C; it is not the O_{P1}(5) summand of F`.
- Degree calculation: `deg(W_f|_C)=4g+12-4f, hence deg(W_5)=16 and deg(W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1})=6 for g=6`.
- Six-point failure locus: `O_C(Gamma) isomorphic to W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}`.
- Derive the failure condition from the f_2=5 summand in SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6, including the sign in gamma^*O(-5).
- Stratify by h^0(W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}).
- Model ordered distinct reduced divisors as a finite etale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open in the relative linear system; do not call that open locus closed.
- Identify components, dimensions, stabilizers, and maps to tetragonal moduli.

## Subproblem graph

- `C66-GEO-Z` (geometry): Construct and identify the evaluation-failure locus Z. Dependencies: none.
- `C66-GEO-H0` (geometry): Stratify the relative degree-six linear system by h0. Dependencies: C66-GEO-Z.
- `C66-GEO-COMP` (geometry): Determine components, dimensions, stabilizers, and finite-cover behavior. Dependencies: C66-GEO-Z, C66-GEO-H0.
- `C66-TATE-SUPPORT` (weakest-sufficient-proof): Prove Tate type for the exact codimension-13 contribution supported on Z. Dependencies: C66-GEO-COMP.
- `C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY` (weakest-sufficient-proof): Assemble the tetragonal contribution into the exact lowest-weight target. Dependencies: C66-TATE-SUPPORT.
- `C66-CEX-LOCAL` (counterexample): Search Z for a non-Tate local system or motivic summand. Dependencies: C66-GEO-COMP.
- `C66-CEX-SURVIVE` (counterexample): Test survival of a non-Tate candidate in the exact target. Dependencies: C66-CEX-LOCAL.
- `C66-COMP-RANK` (computation): Compute determinantal rank-drop ideals and fibre dimensions. Dependencies: C66-GEO-Z.
- `C66-COMP-COMP` (computation): Test proposed component decompositions. Dependencies: C66-GEO-H0.

## Adjudicated findings

- `FND-0001` [mechanically_verified; {'cases': 'all'}]: For d=3g-3+n, the open input is W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_g,n), identified by Poincare duality with W_{2d-16}H^{2d-16}(M_g,n)(d).
- `FND-0005` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: The proposed evaluation-failure locus Z is nonempty by the indicated Riemann-Roch computation, so the empty-locus repair route should be retired if independently confirmed.
- `FND-0020` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: R^1 pi_* Q for the universal n-punctured curve is mixed of weights 1 and 2 (an extension of a rank n-1 Tate system of weight 2 by the rank 2g weight-1 system), never pure of weight 1. The correct weight floor is therefore H^p(base;L) of weight >= p+1, so at p=2d-k-1 the relevant graded piece is Gr^W_{p+1}, and any 'W_p' group named at that spot is identically zero. Attempts that describe the punctured-curve system as pure of weight 1 will be off by exactly one unit of weight and will target a zero group. ATT-0011 exhibits this error in section 2 while stating the correct description in section 5.
- `FND-0022` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: A gonality or Brill-Noether stratification of M_{g,n-1} does not by itself bound the pure-weight cohomology of a local system on the total space: one needs the localization spectral sequence with the correct codimension shifts and Tate twists (in genus 6 the hyperelliptic locus has codimension 4 in M_6, contributing via degree p-8 cohomology of the stratum twisted by Q(-4)) together with control of its differentials. Evaluating only the open stratum is insufficient, since restriction to it is in general neither injective nor surjective. ATT-0011 supplies no shift, twist, or differential bookkeeping, and its stratification is additionally mislabelled: for g=6 gonality takes only values 2, 3, 4, the posited residual Brill-Noether strata are not separate gonality strata, and the gonality-4 open contains the Brill-Noether-special plane quintic locus.
- `FND-0031` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: In the Deligne weight spectral sequence of (Mbar_{g,n}, boundary), the corner gr^W_{2d-16}H^{2d-16}(M_{g,n}) computing the RED-0001 open input sits at spectral-sequence depth m = weight - degree = 0. Hence only the m=0 term H^{2d-16}(Mbar_{g,n}) and the single d_1 Gysin map from the codimension-one strata H^{2d-18}(D^{(1)})(-1) can contribute; strata of codimension >= 2, multi-edge stable graphs, and higher differentials (E_2-degeneration) are all irrelevant to this corner. Dualizing, the resulting cokernel is identical to the boundary sequence of THM-0003, so the weight spectral sequence and the Getzler-Kapranov graph complex yield no information beyond THM-0003 at this corner and cannot break the circularity: they express the open input in terms of the still-unknown H^{16}(Mbar_{g,n}). Any attempt of this approach type must add an independent input for the m=0 term or attack a different corner.
- `FND-0032` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: The CGP / tropical-moduli / commutative-graph-complex computation controls gr^W_0 H^*_c(M_{g,n}), equivalently the top-weight piece gr^W_{2d}H^*(M_{g,n}), whereas the RED-0001 open input W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16} = gr^W_{2d-16}H^{2d-16}(M_{g,n})(d) is the LOWEST weight in its degree (H^{2d-16} of a smooth d-fold has weights in [2d-16, 2d]). The two corners coincide only when 2d = 2d-16, i.e. never. For (6,6), d=21: CGP computes weight 42, the target is weight 26. No twist or dimension-shift bookkeeping can reconcile them, so 'match the CGP degree index to the target' is not an unwritten reference chain but an impossible identification; the undecorated top-weight regime is never the surviving corner for any pair in RED-0001.
- `FND-0033` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: The RED-0001 target W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{g,n}) is a PURE polarizable Q-Hodge structure of weight -16, and the entire weight-(2d-16) row of the E_1 page is pure of that single weight. Since polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of a fixed weight form a semisimple abelian category, any subquotient of a direct sum of Tate objects in that row is again a direct sum of the same Tate object. Consequently there is no non-split-extension obstruction and no semisimplification-versus-actual-isomorphism gap in this corner: proving Tate type on the associated graded of the contributing terms is already an honest Hodge-structure isomorphism. Attempts should not spend a gap marker on ruling out exotic extensions here, and reviewers should not credit such a gap as substantive.
- `FND-0034` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: For (g,n)=(6,6) the non-separating boundary divisor has normalization Mbar_{5,8}, not Mbar_{5,7} as ATT-0014 states: the genus drops by one and the normalization gains TWO legs at the node, 6+2=8, and dim Mbar_{5,8} = 3*5-3+8 = 20 = 21-1 confirms codimension one while dim Mbar_{5,7} = 19 does not. This matters beyond arithmetic: combined with the depth-one restriction above, the only Gysin source into H^{26}(Mbar_{6,6}) other than separating-divisor products is Mbar_{5,8}, and (5,8) is itself an unresolved pair in RED-0001. Any depth-one attack on (6,6) therefore couples directly to the (5,8) case rather than to strictly simpler discharged inputs, and the correct edge-decorated E_1 term is (H^*(Mbar_Gamma) tensor det E_Gamma)^{Aut(Gamma)} -- the determinant twist on the edge set, omitted by ATT-0014, kills contributions whose automorphisms permute edges oddly or swap the two branches of the non-separating node.
- `FND-0035` [corroborated; {'cases': 'RED-0001 residual list', 'coefficients': 'Q'}]: For the RED-0001 residual list, the required ordinary degree 2d-16 equals vcd for (3,12),(5,8),(6,6),(7,4),(8,2) and equals vcd-1 for (8,0),(8,1). It never exceeds vcd, so vanishing-above-vcd proves none of the seven cases; no arbitrary-puncture top-vcd vanishing theorem is asserted.
- `FND-0036` [mechanically_verified; {'degree': 26, 'map': 'M_6,6 to M_6,5'}]: For the forgetful map M_6,6 to M_6,5, the q=0 term H^26(M_6,5;Q) vanishes because 26 exceeds vcd(M_6,5)=25; with fibre cohomology only in q=0,1, no Leray differential enters or leaves total degree 26.
- `FND-0037` [corroborated; {'local_system': 'mixed R^1', 'map': 'M_6,6 to M_6,5'}]: After q=0 vanishing, the exact target is controlled by the mixed R^1 local system. Although its weight-two quotient has no Gr^W_26 H^25 contribution, the connecting map from Gr^W_26 H^24 of that quotient can alter the quotient of Gr^W_26 H^25 of the weight-one symplectic part; this extension effect remains unresolved.
- `FND-0046` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: A fibrewise equivalence between nonvanishing of a CE obstruction space and triviality of a degree-zero line bundle establishes equality only on geometric points. Identifying the relative evaluation-failure locus with an Abel–Jacobi incidence locus over an arbitrary base additionally requires comparison of their determinantal/Fitting scheme structures.
- `FND-0047` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: When h^0(L) jumps, a relative linear system cannot be identified without qualification with Proj of π_*L; one must use a compatible divisor/Hilbert or Abel–Jacobi construction or prove cohomology-and-base-change hypotheses.
- `FND-0048` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: For M_{6,6}, the pure piece W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)=im(H^{26}(\overline M_{6,6};Q)->H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)) is not identified by any supplied argument with a codimension-13 decorated stable-graph complex generated by algebraic cotangent and gluing classes; treating that image as a subquotient of such a complex is circular and does not rule out surviving non-Tate pure weight-26 summands.
- `FND-0050` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: Any complete attack on the exact lowest-weight target for (g,n)=(6,6) must still confront the packet residual geometry (balanced tetragonal splitting, W_5 failure locus Z, h^0 stratification, components/stabilizers); ATT-0020 omits all stable-pair and evaluation-failure analysis and therefore cannot certify absence of a surviving non-Tate summand.
- `FND-0051` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: If boundary contributions are organized by stable graphs, the passage between stacky strata, coarse moduli, and Aut(Γ)-invariants versus coinvariants (with Q coefficients) must be stated; ATT-0020 writes an alternating Gysin complex with no automorphism bookkeeping, so even a corrected strata spectral sequence would be incomplete.
- `FND-0052` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: For the (6,6) CE evaluation-failure locus, the balanced reduced-support relative linear system over the Hurwitz space is an open piece of the failure locus, not a closed pure-codimension-4 subvariety of M_{6,6}; Gysin for (M_{6,6},Z) requires a closed (stratified) embedding after h^0 and splitting-type stratification.
- `FND-0053` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: That S_6 has rational irreducible representations does not imply that an S_6-cover of a relative configuration/linear-system space carries only Tate local systems; geometric monodromy of the tetragonal family and configuration-space coefficients can still produce non-Tate summands.
- `FND-0054` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: Declaring the genus-6 balanced tetragonal Hurwitz space ‘rational/Tate’ and deducing pure-Tate cohomology of Z upgrades a predicted/possible motive to an unconditional theorem and is not a substitute for C66-TATE-SUPPORT.
- `FND-0055` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: Vanishing of H^0(C,ω⊗W_5^∨(Γ)) on the complementary open U does not by itself force W_26 H^{26}(U) (or lowest-weight BM of U) to be pure Tate; CE syzygy vanishing is not a purity theorem for open moduli cohomology.
- `FND-0057` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: A claimed_complete C66-FULL argument with proof_dependencies=[] and no_undischarged_dependencies=true is inconsistent with the campaign graph requiring GEO-Z→GEO-H0→GEO-COMP→TATE-SUPPORT→TATE-ASSEMBLY before assembly into the exact target.
- `FND-0058` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: On the balanced tetragonal stack for (g,n)=(6,6), the identification of the CE evaluation-failure locus with a relative P^2-bundle |ω_C(-D)| (fiber dimension exactly 2) requires proof that h^0(ω_C(-D))=1+h^0(D) is constantly 3 on the whole balanced locus, not merely for general tetragonal curves; without that, pure dimension 17 and codimension 4 in M_{6,6} are not established.
- `FND-0060` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: The count dim H_6^{tet,bal}=b-3=15 is a coarse moduli dimension for branched covers modulo Aut(P^1); promoting it to the dimension of a moduli stack of balanced tetragonal curves with marked points, and to codimension inside the stack M_{6,6}, requires a stabilizer/automorphism analysis that ATT-0022 omits.
- `FND-0061` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: Degree and Serre-duality control of H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_f^vee(Γ)) for f=4,5 is not by itself a complete identification of the Casnati–Ekedahl evaluation-failure locus unless those groups are shown to be exactly the obstruction spaces of the CE evaluation map (packet: derive failure from the f_2=5 summand of SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6).
- `FND-0062` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: On any smooth genus-6 degree-four cover C -> P^1 with balanced splitting F = O(4) ⊕ O(5), the f=4 component of the CE evaluation obstruction bundle \omega_C \otimes W_4^\vee(\Gamma) has degree -4 for any degree-six divisor \Gamma, hence H^0(\omega_C \otimes W_4^\vee(\Gamma)) = 0 and the obstruction vanishes identically on this component.
- `FND-0063` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}}]: On any smooth genus-6 degree-four cover C -> P^1 with balanced splitting F = O(4) ⊕ O(5), the f=5 component of the CE evaluation obstruction bundle \omega_C \otimes W_5^\vee(\Gamma) has degree 0 for any degree-six divisor \Gamma.
